policy.scope: source-bound normalization, desugaring, control-flow lowering, representation lowering, and shared MIR emission
policy.foreign_suffix: target ABI, foreign libraries, runtime resources, and finite behavioral replay remain explicit downstream boundaries

claim.statement: Each production normalization, desugaring, control-flow lowering, and representation pass is joined to the canonical checked TIR/MIR route and carries a conditional preservation certificate. The certificate retains source origin, side conditions, and the complete observation alphabet; it is not a universal semantic proof.
preconditions: The #2898/#2919 canonical operation denominator is read from the generated compiler obligation relation; this stage adds no second lowerer or operation denominator.
The checked sema-to-TIR-to-MIR route is the only lowering route named by a certificate.
Source identity, source order, typed failures, mutation, input consumption, cleanup, and target applicability are explicit premises.
A lowering rejection remains a rejection through the shared semantic route; a source, IR, target, or certificate mismatch is invalid evidence.
Unknown compiler observations, unavailable targets, and foreign suffixes remain unverified rather than proved.
unsupported_cases: A missing, stale, or unbound production pass certificate
A source/IR/target identity mismatch or a certificate attached to a different operation
A reordered effect or failure, extra input consumption, invalid alias premise, or unchecked arithmetic reassociation
A target cost decision used to legalize an otherwise illegal transformation
Universal preservation over every Jet source, MIR state, target ABI, resource schedule, or foreign implementation
A fresh compiler replay or behavioral qualification when the pinned compiler is unavailable

execution.crash_policy: tool failures, unavailable binaries, and malformed responses are unavailable or invalid_oracle, never preservation

binding_methods.implementation: checked sema/TIR lowering and the single TIR-to-MIR seam
binding_methods.construction: source-bound operation relation with exact implementation symbol, origin, premises, observations, and target contract
binding_methods.limit: construction binding is not a universal preservation theorem

binding_methods.implementation: the production checked-TIR-to-MIR route and canonical MIR emitter
binding_methods.candidate_binding: current source SHA-256, compiler-proof identity, target/configuration descriptors
binding_methods.limit: no compiler or Jet execution is performed by this source checker

binding_methods.certificate: every generated production operation, legal/invalid source witness, composition premise, negative control, and optional canonical TIR/MIR route observation
binding_methods.limit: finite route observations remain proof-blocking until an independently derived semantic goal has a pinned formal discharge

selection: canonical TExprKind and TStmt operation rows
#2898.rule: reuse the generated operation denominator; do not add a lowering-specific semantic engine

#2919.rule: bind every production pass to the current sema/TIR/MIR implementation route

coverage.qualification_rule: A boundary remains blocked unless every current production pass has a current source binding, complete premises, and matched canonical route observations; no finite route observation is promoted to semantic legality or proof without an independent formal discharge.

implementation_route.single_route_rule: No engine-specific semantic lowering is introduced; all targets consume the canonical checked MIR and retain target facts at the emission boundary.

proven: The checker joins the exact generated canonical operation relation to the current #2939 lowering boundary.
Every registered production lowering pass requires implementation identity, origin identity, side conditions, all observations, and separate legality/profitability fields.
Forged, reordered, over-consuming, aliased, unsound, cost-overriding, and wrong-operation certificates are rejected structurally.
Composition requires the ordered pass relation and preserves observations, origin, side conditions, legality, profitability, and target representation.
assumed: D-TIER-ONEIR1, D-COMPILER-PROOF1, I3, and I9 define the shared checked route.
#2898 supplies the canonical operation denominator and #2919 supplies the current integrated implementation route.
Foreign compiler, target ABI/layout, allocator/resource schedule, and external callback environments satisfy their named contracts.
tested: Legal and deliberately invalid witness sources are source-hash bound and kept distinct without executing them.
Source/IR/target mismatch checks, premise retention, and negative-control mutation sensitivity are exercised by the checker logic.
blocked: Universal preservation for all source programs, MIR states, target layouts, failures, effects, schedules, and resource bounds.
Fresh compiler execution, replay of AOT/JIT/interpreter/check observations, and qualification of cost or foreign behavior.
A generated operation row with stale source identity or missing observation evidence.
